title: Data Structures & Algorithms (Problem Solving)
description: Rigorous mastery of DSA patterns for software engineering interviews: Big-O, two-pointers, sliding window, fast/slow pointers, monotonic stacks, backtracking, binary search, trees, graphs, 1D/2D dynamic programming, and tries.

phases.title: Complexity & Linear Data Structures
phases.focus: Big-O Analysis, Two-Pointers, Sliding Window, Linked Lists & Monotonic Stacks

phases.title: Trees, Recursion & Core Algorithms
phases.focus: Backtracking, Hash Tables, Advanced Binary Search, Trees/BFS/DFS & Heaps

phases.title: Graphs, DP & Advanced Structures
phases.focus: Shortest Paths, 1D & 2D Dynamic Programming, Intervals, Tries & Disjoint Set Union

phases.title: Mastery & Technical Interview Capstone
phases.focus: Pattern Recognition Taxonomy, Space-Time Trade-offs & Timed Interview Mastery

nodes.title: Complexity Analysis & Big-O Foundations
nodes.subtitle: Time vs Space complexity, asymptotic analysis (O, Omega, Theta), amortized analysis, recursion tree
learning_objectives: Calculate exact Big-O time and space complexity for iterative and recursive algorithms
Analyze amortized time complexity for dynamic arrays and hash tables
feynman_prompts: Explain the difference between O(1) amortized insertion and O(N) worst-case insertion in a dynamic array.
key_misconceptions: Assuming that fewer lines of code automatically equals faster Big-O execution time

nodes.title: Arrays, Strings & Two-Pointer Techniques
nodes.subtitle: Opposite-direction pointers, same-direction pointers, palindrome verification, trapped rainwater, in-place swaps
learning_objectives: Apply two-pointer patterns to solve search and partition problems in O(N) time and O(1) space
Solve classic problems: Two Sum II, Container With Most Water, In-place Duplicate Removal
feynman_prompts: Why is the two-pointer approach optimal for sorted array target search compared to nested loops?
key_misconceptions: Allocating extra array memory when an in-place two-pointer swap is achievable

nodes.title: Sliding Window & Prefix Sum Patterns
nodes.subtitle: Fixed-size window, dynamic-size window, subarray sum equals K, longest substring without repeats
learning_objectives: Maintain running window state to solve dynamic contiguous subarray and substring problems
Precompute prefix sum arrays to answer range sum queries in O(1) time
feynman_prompts: Explain how the sliding window technique reduces an O(N^2) brute-force check to O(N) linear time.
key_misconceptions: Recomputing entire window sums from scratch instead of adding incoming and subtracting outgoing elements

nodes.title: Linked Lists & Fast/Slow Pointer Pattern
nodes.subtitle: Singly/doubly linked lists, cycle detection (Floyd's algorithm), middle of list, list reversal
learning_objectives: Reverse singly and doubly linked lists iteratively and recursively in O(1) auxiliary space
Detect cycles and locate cycle entry points using Floyd's Tortoise and Hare algorithm
feynman_prompts: Why does Floyd's fast/slow pointer algorithm guarantee meeting inside a cycle?
key_misconceptions: Losing reference pointers during node swaps, causing memory leaks or infinite loops

nodes.title: Stacks, Queues & Monotonic Stack Patterns
nodes.subtitle: LIFO/FIFO mechanics, parentheses matching, monotonic increasing/decreasing stacks, next greater element
learning_objectives: Utilize monotonic stacks to find Next Greater Element and Largest Rectangle in Histogram in O(N)
Implement queue functionality using two stacks with amortized O(1) operations
feynman_prompts: Explain how a monotonic stack maintains sorted order while finding nearest greater elements.
key_misconceptions: Using nested loops to search for next greater elements, resulting in O(N^2) timeouts

nodes.title: Recursion & Combinatorial Backtracking
nodes.subtitle: Recursion stack, call frames, permutations, subsets, combination sum, N-Queens, pruning state trees
learning_objectives: Model problem search spaces as state trees and prune invalid search paths early
Generate all permutations, subsets, and combinations with correct backtracking state restoration
feynman_prompts: What is backtracking state restoration and why must changes be undone after the recursive call?
key_misconceptions: Passing copies of large arrays at every recursion step instead of backtracking in-place

nodes.title: Hash Tables & Hash Map Optimization
nodes.subtitle: Hash functions, collision resolution (chaining vs open addressing), load factor, amortized lookup
learning_objectives: Analyze how hash table resizing and load factor impact amortized O(1) operations
Leverage hash maps and sets for frequency counting and O(1) membership lookups
feynman_prompts: What happens to hash table performance when a bad hash function produces frequent collisions?
key_misconceptions: Assuming hash table operations are strictly O(1) in the worst-case (they degrade to O(N))

nodes.title: Binary Search & Search Space Reduction
nodes.subtitle: Binary search template, search in rotated sorted array, binary search on answer space (Koko eating bananas)
learning_objectives: Apply binary search templates avoiding off-by-one errors (left <= right vs left < right)
Solve optimization problems using binary search on answer spaces (monotonic feasibility functions)
feynman_prompts: How do you recognize when a problem can be solved by binary search on the answer space?
key_misconceptions: Calculating midpoint using `(left + right) / 2` which can cause integer overflow in languages like C++/Java

nodes.title: Binary Trees & Tree Traversals (DFS / BFS)
nodes.subtitle: Pre/in/post-order traversals, level-order BFS, BST properties, Lowest Common Ancestor (LCA), diameter
learning_objectives: Implement iterative and recursive DFS and queue-based BFS level-order traversals
Validate binary search trees and find lowest common ancestors in O(H) time
feynman_prompts: Why does an in-order traversal of a Binary Search Tree always yield values in sorted order?
key_misconceptions: Confusing binary trees with binary search trees

nodes.title: Heaps & Priority Queues (Top-K Patterns)
nodes.subtitle: Min-heap vs max-heap, heapify, finding Kth largest, median of a data stream, merge K sorted lists
learning_objectives: Solve Top-K frequent elements and streaming median problems in O(N log K) time
Construct heaps from raw arrays in O(N) linear time using bottom-up heapify
feynman_prompts: Why does building a heap take O(N) time while inserting N elements one-by-one takes O(N log N)?
key_misconceptions: Sorting an entire array of N elements in O(N log N) when only top K elements are needed

nodes.title: Graph Foundations & Traversals (BFS / DFS)
nodes.subtitle: Adjacency matrix vs list, connected components, cycle detection in directed/undirected graphs, bipartite graphs
learning_objectives: Traverse directed and undirected graphs using BFS and DFS while tracking visited states
Detect cycles in directed graphs using 3-color DFS (unvisited, visiting, visited)
feynman_prompts: What happens if you forget to mark nodes as visited during graph BFS or DFS?
key_misconceptions: Assuming graphs are always connected or acyclic without checking

nodes.title: Shortest Paths & Topological Sort
nodes.subtitle: Dijkstra's algorithm, Kahn's algorithm (topological sort), course schedule, Bellman-Ford basics
learning_objectives: Implement Dijkstra's algorithm with a priority queue to find shortest paths in weighted graphs
Detect dependency cycles and establish build orders using Kahn's topological sort
feynman_prompts: Why does Dijkstra's algorithm fail when edges have negative weights?
key_misconceptions: Attempting to use simple BFS to find shortest paths on graphs with varying edge weights

nodes.title: Dynamic Programming: 1D Memoization & Tabulation
nodes.subtitle: Optimal substructure, overlapping subproblems, top-down memoization vs bottom-up tabulation, space optimization
learning_objectives: Identify optimal substructure and overlapping subproblems in recursive formulations
Transition from exponential recursion to linear O(N) DP with O(1) space optimization (Climbing Stairs, House Robber)
feynman_prompts: Explain how memoization eliminates redundant recursive recalculations.
key_misconceptions: Memorizing solutions without writing down the explicit mathematical recurrence relation first

nodes.title: Dynamic Programming: 2D Grids & Strings
nodes.subtitle: Grid paths, Longest Common Subsequence (LCS), Edit Distance, 0/1 Knapsack, unbounded knapsack
learning_objectives: Solve 2D grid pathfinding and string edit distance problems using 2D tabulation matrices
Optimize 2D dynamic programming memory consumption from O(M*N) to O(N) rolling arrays
feynman_prompts: Walk through the recurrence relation for Edit Distance (Insert, Delete, Replace).
key_misconceptions: Mixing up row and column indices when referencing prior subproblem states

nodes.title: Interval Scheduling & Greedy Algorithms
nodes.subtitle: Interval merging, meeting rooms, non-overlapping intervals, greedy choice property vs DP
learning_objectives: Sort intervals by start or end times to solve interval overlap and consolidation problems
Determine when a greedy local choice guarantees global optimality versus when DP is required
feynman_prompts: Why must intervals be sorted by end time in the activity selection greedy algorithm?
key_misconceptions: Assuming a greedy algorithm works without proving the greedy-choice property

nodes.title: Trie (Prefix Tree) & String Matching
nodes.subtitle: Trie node architecture, insert/search/startsWith, autocomplete, Word Search II, KMP overview
learning_objectives: Build prefix trees (Trie) supporting O(L) prefix search, auto-completion, and wildcard matching
Combine Tries with backtracking DFS to solve multi-word grid search problems efficiently
feynman_prompts: Why is a Trie faster than a hash set for prefix queries like 'startsWith(str)'?
key_misconceptions: Creating unindexed string slices repeatedly, resulting in severe memory allocation

nodes.title: Disjoint Set Union (DSU) & Union-Find
nodes.subtitle: Find with path compression, Union by rank/size, Kruskal's Minimum Spanning Tree, redundant connections
learning_objectives: Implement Disjoint Set Union with path compression and union by rank achieving near O(1) alpha(N)
Detect redundant graph connections and find Minimum Spanning Trees using Kruskal's algorithm
feynman_prompts: Explain how path compression flattens the tree during find operations to achieve amortized O(1).
key_misconceptions: Performing naive union operations without tracking tree rank, creating degenerate O(N) linked lists

nodes.title: Advanced Problem-Solving Strategy & Interview Mastery
nodes.subtitle: Pattern recognition taxonomy, space-time trade-offs, edge-case checklist, mock interview performance
learning_objectives: Rapidly categorize unseen problems into core algorithmic patterns within 3 minutes
Write clean, bug-free, production-quality code under timed interview pressure with full test verification
feynman_prompts: How do you systematically debug a failing test case during a live coding technical interview?
key_misconceptions: Jumping immediately into writing code before dry-running edge cases and stating complexity
